payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show genuine progress toward placing the same source book behind the same source rose, even if the requested placement is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass only if identifiable source objects show a changed relative placement or other clear visual evidence of movement toward the book-behind-rose relation, without establishing complete fulfillment. Fail if the identifiable objects clearly show no such progress. Unknown if identity or progress cannot be determined. Changes to object appearance or unrelated objects alone are not progress.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images to track the source blue-covered book and rose. Judge progress toward their requested depth relation, not merely whether either object changed; use visible relative placement and depth cues, without requiring overlap when other clear evidence supports progress.

node_traces.evidence: The source blue-covered book and rose are identifiable, but the edited image shows the blue book still separate from the flowers and no clear movement toward placing it behind the source rose. The edited flowers also appear different from the source rose, so they do not establish progress on the requested relation.

The flowers also appear changed, but appearance changes alone do not establish the requested placement progress.

fulfillment: The binding is underspecified and inconsistent: it alternates between “flower” and the source rose, while the edited image contains two yellow flowers and the source has one red-yellow rose. Make the node explicitly assess the requested book–source-flower relation, using both supports’ evidence about object identity and visible depth/occlusion; do not treat a changed or ambiguous flower as proof that the relation is absent. Distinguish clear evidence of no progress (e.g., identifiable objects remain separate) from inability to match the source flower, which should remain unresolved unless the other support independently establishes absence. Preserve the partial-progress criterion: assess visible movement toward the requested placement, not merely whether the final relation is complete. The repeated high-confidence failures support the no label, but the single unknown is a valid evidence/identity ambiguity, not a transport failure; avoid forcing agreement by suppressing unknowns. Ensure the executable binding carries the same precise target and criteria as the node’s full specification.
